summary: This short RFC creates an IANA registry for response codes used by the MEDIACTRL Interactive Voice Response Control Package, which was described in RFC 6231.

eli5.summary: It makes a public list that keeps track of the answer codes used by a phone menu control system, so everyone uses the same ones.

subtitle: A short IANA registry that gives the voice-menu control protocol's response codes an official home.

tldr.problem: RFC 6231 defined status codes for the MEDIACTRL Interactive Voice Response (IVR) Control Package, but there was no IANA registry to record them or to govern new ones.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6623 has IANA create the 'MEDIACTRL Interactive Voice Response Control Package Status Codes' registry, fills it with the codes from RFC 6231, and says new codes need Standards Action.
tldr.outcome: The codes now live in one public registry, and adding to it requires a standards-track process. The RFC is a Proposed Standard and updates RFC 6231.

facts.label: Registry name
facts.value: MEDIACTRL Interactive Voice Response Control Package Status Codes

today: RFC 6623 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6231, and no later RFC obsoletes it. It remains the document that created the status code registry.

sections.title: What the RFC Does
sections.content:
RFC 6623 is a very small housekeeping document. Its only job is to create an IANA registry for the response codes of the MEDIACTRL Interactive Voice Response Control Package, which is described in RFC 6231.

The package is used to control interactive voice response (IVR) dialogs on the server that executes requests, which the codes call the MS. When the MS answers a request, it reports a numeric status code. Before this RFC, those codes were listed only inside RFC 6231.
sections.eli5: A phone-menu system answers with number codes. This document just writes those codes down in one official list.

sections.title: The New Registry and Its Rules
sections.content:
Section 3 says that IANA has created a registry named MEDIACTRL Interactive Voice Response Control Package Status Codes. Each entry has four columns: Code, Summary, Description and Reference.

New status codes are assigned using the Standards Action process defined in RFC 5226. In practice, a new code needs a standards-track document behind it, not just a request to IANA.

The acknowledgements note that the table was lifted directly from the text written by the authors of RFC 6231, and that any transcription errors are the new author's. Every row therefore points back to RFC 6231 as its reference.
sections.eli5: The list has a rule for adding new numbers: you have to go through the official standards process first, so nobody can sneak one in.

sections.title: The Status Codes
sections.content:
The table starts with 200 (OK, the request has succeeded) and 400 (a syntax error: the request is not valid against the XML schema, or breaks a co-occurrence constraint for a request element).

Codes 405 to 413 report problems with identifiers and resources. For example, 405 means a dialogid is already used by another dialog on the MS, 406, 407 and 408 mean a dialog, connection or conference identifier does not exist, 409 means an external resource could not be retrieved within the timeout interval, and 410 means the dialog was already terminated by a <dialogterminate>.

Codes 411 and 412 cover media stream problems: a configuration that conflicts with itself or with the connection or conference capabilities, and an operation for which no suitable media stream is available, such as playing video on a connection with no video streams. Code 413 flags a <control> element where some keys have the same value.
sections.eli5: Each number means a different thing, like 200 for 'all good' and 400-something for 'I could not do that, and here is why'.

sections.title: Unsupported Capabilities
sections.content:
Most of the remaining codes tell the sender that the MS cannot do what was asked. Code 419 is the catch-all for other execution errors, and 439 is the catch-all for another unsupported capability.

In between are specific refusals: 420 unsupported URI scheme, 421 unsupported dialog language, 422 unsupported playback format, 423 unsupported record format and 424 unsupported grammar format. Codes 425 to 430 reject individual elements or configurations: a prompt <variable>, a prompt <dtmf>, a <param>, a <stream> configuration, a <prompt> that cannot be played and a <record> that cannot be recorded.

The last specific codes cover optional features. Code 431 is for foreign namespace attributes or elements, 432 for starting another dialog where one is already running, 433 for <collect> and <record> used together, 434 for a record request that requires Voice Activity Detection (VAD) when the MS lacks it, and 435 for an unsupported prompt <par> element.
sections.eli5: When the machine cannot do something you asked, it tells you exactly what it cannot do, like 'I cannot play that kind of sound file'.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: RFC 6623 adds nothing new here. It says there are no security considerations other than those already described in RFC 6231, the control package itself.
sections.eli5: Making a list of codes does not create new dangers, so the only safety rules are the ones that already existed.
